folktale_excerpt: A peasant in Holl had a servant girl whom no one knew. She was very industrious and well behaved, but she would not say what her name was. One day the man was carrying a yoke home from the field when the voice of an unseen person called out to him several times, 'You, the man carrying the yoke, tell Gloria that the chancellor has died.' parable_title: When Jeroboam erected the two golden calves, they… (Mid. Songs 1)

There was near by an old man, named Abbé Kolon, who told the builders that unless water were brought from the river Euphrates to Mix With the lime, no building would stand there, and he offered to fetch the water from the Euphrates. He took large casks, and posing as a wine merchant made his way unopposed to the river Euphrates, where he filled his casks with water of that river and returned to Rome. The water being used for the mixing of the lime and sand, the houses were successfully erected.

folktale_title: The Fisher and the Little Fish
folktale_excerpt: It happened that a fisher, after fishing all day, caught only a little fish. 'Pray, let me go, master,' said the fish. 'I am much too small for you to eat just now. A little thing in hand is worth more than a great thing in prospect.

folktale_title: There Is No Difference between Youth and Old Age
folktale_atu_name: Human and Animal Life Spans Are Readjusted (previously Men and Animals Readjust Span of Life)
folktale_excerpt: One day the Hodja said, 'There is no difference between youth and old age.' Someone asked him, 'How so?' He answered, 'In front of our door there is a stone so heavy that only a few people are able to lift it. In my youth I attempted to do so, but was unable to. Later, now that I am an old man, I remembered this, and attempted once again, but was still unable to lift it. This experience is why I say that there is no difference between youth and old age.'

folktale_excerpt: There was a frightful drought. The rivers after a while dried up and even the springs gave no water. The animals wandered around seeking drink, but to no avail. parable_title: The Return of the Unclean Spirit (Matthew 12:43-45)
parable_excerpt: “When an unclean spirit has gone out of a man, he passes through waterless places seeking rest, and doesn’t find it. Then he says, ‘I will return into my house from which I came;’ and when he has come back, he finds it empty, swept, and put in order. Then he goes and takes with himself seven other spirits more evil than he is, and they enter in and dwell there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first. Even so will it be also to this evil generation.”
